Name: Thiruvarangam
Note: The first Divya Desam, called simply Koil, "the Temple". Eleven Azhwars sang here, and Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu stayed four months of Caturmasya.

Name: Thirukkozhi
Note: Birthplace of Thiruppaan Azhwar. The Thayar has precedence here, and Namperumal of Srirangam comes as the bridegroom each Panguni.

Name: Thirukkarambanur
Note: One compound holds shrines of Vishnu, Shiva and Brahma with their consorts, so it is also called the Trimurti kshetram.

Name: Thiruvellarai
Note: Tradition holds it older than Srirangam. Two gateways are used by season, one for Uttarayana and one for Dakshinayana.

Name: Thiru Anbil
Note: A quiet village shrine across the Kollidam from Koviladi, sung in a single verse by Thirumazhisai Azhwar.

Name: Thirupper Nagar
Note: The Lord rests with a pot of appam by His hand. Nammazhwar's last decad on an earthly temple (Thiruvaimozhi 10.8) was sung here.

Name: Thirukkandiyur
Note: Here the Lord freed Shiva from the curse of Brahma's skull that had stuck to his hand, hence the name.

Name: Thirukkoodalur
Note: The devas gathered (koodal) here to pray when the earth was carried away, and the Lord protected the world.

Name: Thirukkavithalam
Note: The place of Gajendra moksha in local tradition, and one of the five Krishnaranya kshetrams.

Name: Thiruppullam Bhoothangudi
Note: Sri Rama rests here after performing the last rites for Jatayu, a rare reclining Rama.

Name: Thiru Adanur
Note: The Lord lies with a grain measure as His pillow and a stylus and palm leaf in hand, the keeper of every account.

Name: Thirukkudanthai
Note: Nathamuni heard the "Aravamude" decad sung here and went in search of the lost four thousand verses. The whole Divya Prabandham was recovered because of this temple.

Name: Thiruvinnagar
Note: All offerings are cooked without salt, in memory of the Lord's promise to the young Bhumi Devi's father, Markandeya.

Name: Thirunaraiyur
Note: The Lord Himself gave pancha-samskara to Thirumangai Azhwar here. Thayar leads every procession, and the stone Kal Garuda grows heavier at each gate.

Name: Thirucherai
Note: Pancha Sara kshetram: the Lord, Thayar, vimanam, tank and town all bear the name Sara. River Kaveri did penance here.

Name: Thirukkannamangai
Note: The devas are said to remain as bees in the hive at the Thayar shrine, to keep seeing the divine wedding.

Name: Thirukkannapuram
Note: Kulasekhara Azhwar's lullaby to Sri Rama, "Mannu pugazh Kosalai", is addressed to the Lord of this town.

Name: Thirukkannangudi
Note: Krishna was bound here by the affection of sage Vasishtha. Many Thirumangai Azhwar stories are told about its tree, well and field.

Name: Thirunagai
Note: Thirumangai Azhwar, speaking as a girl in love, can only repeat "acho oruvar azhagiyava", what a beauty!

Name: Thanjai Mamani Koil
Note: Three neighbouring temples are counted as one Divya Desam. The Lord ended the demon Tanjaka here, which gave Thanjavur its name.

Name: Thirunandipura Vinnagaram
Note: Nandi was freed from a curse here. The kshetram is also called Dakshina Jagannatham.

Name: Thiruvelliyangudi
Note: Sukra (Velli) regained his sight here. Garuda in this temple uniquely holds the conch and discus.

Name: Thiruvazhundur
Note: Krishna stands as the cowherd Amaruviappan with a cow and calf. It is also the birthplace of the poet Kambar.

Name: Thiruchirupuliyur
Note: The Lord reclines here in a small, child-sized form (bala sayanam) at the request of sage Vyaghrapada.

Name: Thalaichanga Nanmadiyam
Note: Chandra, the moon, was relieved of his curse here, and the Lord wears the crescent.

Name: Thiruvindalur
Note: A place of Ekadasi glory. Thirumangai Azhwar, finding the doors shut, scolds the Lord lovingly in his verses.

Name: Thirukkavalambadi
Thayar: Madavaral Mangai, with Rukmini and Satyabhama
Note: Krishna stands with Rukmini and Satyabhama. Tradition links the grove to the parijata He brought for Satyabhama.

Name: Kazhicheerama Vinnagaram
Note: Trivikrama stands with His left foot raised to measure the worlds. Thirumangai Azhwar won his spear in a poetry contest here.

Name: Arimeya Vinnagaram
Note: Krishna, the dancer with the pots. Sung as the One who lifted Govardhana.

Name: Vanpurushottamam
Note: The Lord gave an ocean of milk to the hungry child Upamanyu here. Associated with Rama of Ayodhya among the Nangur eleven.

Name: Semponsei Koil
Note: Named "the temple made of pure gold". Sri Rama is said to have gifted a golden cow here after the war.

Name: Manimada Koil
Note: The eleven Perumals of Nangur assemble here on Garuda the day after Thai Amavasya, with Thirumangai Azhwar greeting each one.

Name: Vaikunta Vinnagaram
Note: The Lord sits as in Paramapadam, with Sri, Bhu and Nila.

Name: Thiruvali Thirunagari
Note: Twin temples counted as one. Thirumangai Azhwar tried to rob a wedding party here, and the Bridegroom gave him the eight-syllable mantra instead.

Name: Thiruthevanar Thogai
Note: The devas gathered here in a crowd (thogai) to see the Lord's wedding with the daughter of the ocean.

Name: Thiruthetriambalam
Note: The only one of the eleven Nangur temples where the Lord reclines, and the only Divya Desam called an ambalam.

Name: Thirumanikkoodam
Note: Linked with Varadaraja of Kanchi among the Nangur eleven. Chandra worshipped here.

Name: Thiruvellakkulam
Note: Called the elder brother (Annan) of Tirumala's Lord. Kumudavalli, who turned Thirumangai Azhwar to devotion, appeared here.

Name: Thirupparthanpalli
Note: Krishna taught and comforted Arjuna (Partha) here, and brought forth water for him.

Name: Thiruchitrakoodam
Note: The Lord reclines inside the great Nataraja temple, watching the cosmic dance. Kulasekhara Azhwar tells the whole Ramayana in his decad on this shrine.

Name: Thiruvahindrapuram
Note: Vedanta Desika meditated on the Oushadagiri hillock here and received the grace of Hayagriva and Garuda.

Name: Thirukkovalur
Note: The three first Azhwars met in a narrow passage on a stormy night, felt a fourth Person pressing among them, and the Divya Prabandham was born.

Name: Thirukkachi Atthigiri
Note: Perumal Koil, where Ramanuja served daily and Thirukachi Nambi fanned the Lord. Athi Varadar, the fig-wood form, is brought out of the tank once in forty years.

Name: Ashtabuyagaram
Note: The Lord stands with eight arms and eight weapons, come to protect Brahma's sacrifice.

Name: Thiruthanka
Note: The Lord appeared as a light to dispel darkness at Brahma's sacrifice. Vedanta Desika was born next door at Thoopul.

Name: Thiruvelukkai
Note: Narasimha chose to stay (vel irukkai, the place He wished to stay) after driving away the demons.

Name: Thiruneeragam
Note: One of four Divya Desams inside the Ulagalantha Perumal compound, sung in a single shared verse.

Name: Thiruppadagam
Note: A towering seated Krishna, showing the universal form He revealed in the Kaurava court as the Pandavas' messenger.

Name: Nilathingal Thundam
Note: A Divya Desam inside a Shiva temple, where the Lord cooled Parvati's penance with moonlight.

Name: Thiruooragam
Note: A Trivikrama about 35 feet tall. He also gives darshan as a serpent (uraga) for Mahabali, who could not take in the huge form.

Name: Thiruvekka
Note: "The Lord who did as He was told." He rolled up His serpent bed and followed Thirumazhisai Azhwar out of the city, then came back and lay down the other way round.

Name: Thirukkaragam
Note: Within the Ulagalantha Perumal compound, named in the same single verse as Neeragam and Karvanam.

Name: Thirukkarvanam
Note: The Lord the colour of a rain cloud, in the Ulagalantha Perumal compound.

Name: Thirukkalvanur
Note: A small shrine inside the Kamakshi temple. The Lord is the "thief" who overheard a conversation between Lakshmi and Parvati.

Name: Thiruppavalavannam
Note: The coral-coloured Lord. Pilgrims pair it with the emerald Pachaivannar temple opposite.

Name: Parameswara Vinnagaram
Note: A Pallava temple of three storeys, with the Lord sitting, reclining and standing one above another.

Name: Thirupputkuzhi
Note: Sri Rama sits holding Jatayu, having performed the bird's last rites here. Ramanuja studied in this village as a boy.

Name: Thirunindravur
Note: Thayar is called "the Mother who bore me". Tradition says She sent the Lord after Thirumangai Azhwar to obtain a verse.

Name: Thiruevvul
Note: The Lord asked sage Salihotra "evvul?", in which room may I rest. Pilgrims pray here for healing, especially on new moon days.

Name: Thiruvallikkeni
Note: Krishna as Arjuna's charioteer, with a moustache and without the discus. The utsavar's face bears the marks of Bhishma's arrows.

Name: Thiruneermalai
Note: The one place to see the Lord standing, sitting, reclining and striding, at the foot and on top of a small hill.

Name: Thiruvidanthai
Place: Thiruvidanthai, East Coast Road (Nitya Kalyana Perumal)
Perumal: Lakshmi Varahan; utsavar Nitya Kalyana Perumal
Note: Varaha holds Bhumi Devi on His left side. The Lord married 360 maidens here, one each day, so every day is a wedding day.

Name: Thirukkadalmallai
Note: The Lord lies on the bare ground without Adisesha, having come to sage Pundarika. Birthplace of Bhoothath Azhwar.

Name: Thirukkadigai
Note: Staying here for one kadigai, about 24 minutes, is said to be enough. Yoga Narasimha is on the big hill and Yoga Anjaneya on the small hill.

Name: Thirunavai
Note: On the bank of the Bharathapuzha. Unusually for Kerala, the Goddess has Her own separate shrine.

Name: Thiruvithuvakkodu
Note: Kulasekhara Azhwar's decad of ten similes of helpless dependence, such as the child who clings to the mother even when she pushes it away.

Name: Thirukkatkarai
Note: The seat of the Onam festival, where Vamana received three paces of land from Mahabali.

Name: Thirumoozhikkalam
Note: Worshipped as Lakshmana in Kerala's Nalambalam circuit of the four brothers of Sri Rama.

Name: Thiruvallavazh
Note: Known for daily Kathakali offered as worship, and for a tall granite flagstaff topped by Garuda.

Name: Thirukkadithanam
Note: One of the five temples linked to the Pandavas, this one to Sahadeva.

Name: Thiruchenkundrur
Note: Linked to Yudhishthira, who is said to have prayed here after the war for having spoken a half-truth.

Name: Thiruppuliyur
Note: Linked to Bhima. Nammazhwar speaks as the friend of a girl who is already wholly given to Mayapiran.

Name: Thiruvaranvilai
Note: Linked to Arjuna. Famous for the Pampa snake boat race and the Aranmula metal mirror.

Name: Thiruvanvandoor
Note: Linked to Nakula. Nammazhwar sends birds as messengers to the Lord in this decad.

Name: Thiruvananthapuram
Note: The Lord is so long that He is seen through three doors: face, navel and feet. Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu had darshan here.

Name: Thiruvattaru
Note: Regarded as the elder of the two great reclining forms of the far south. Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu found the Brahma-samhita in this temple.

Name: Thiruvanparisaram
Note: The home village of Udayanangai, mother of Nammazhwar. Lakshmi dwells on the Lord's chest, so there is no separate Thayar shrine.

Name: Thirukkurungudi
Perumal: Sundara Paripooranan (Vaishnava Nambi): Nindra, Irundha and Kidantha Nambi
Note: The Lord of this town is said to have been born as Nammazhwar. Home of the Kaisika Ekadasi story of Nampaduvan, and where Thirumangai Azhwar spent his last days.

Name: Thirucheeravaramangai
Note: A self-manifest kshetram and seat of the Vanamamalai Mutt. The oil from the Lord's daily abhishekam is collected in a well and taken as medicine.

Name: Thiruvaikuntam
Note: First of the Nava Tirupati on the Tamraparni (Surya). The sun's rays fall on the Lord on two days each year.

Name: Thiruvaragunamangai
Note: Nava Tirupati (Chandra). The Lord sits under the hood of Adisesha.

Name: Thiruppulingudi
Note: Nava Tirupati (Budha). The Lord's feet are seen through a window in the outer wall of the sanctum.

Name: Tholaivillimangalam
Note: Two temples a short walk apart counted as one Divya Desam (Rahu and Ketu). Nammazhwar sings as a mother whose daughter cannot stop gazing towards this place.

Name: Thirukkulanthai
Note: Nava Tirupati (Sani). The Lord danced on the demon He defeated, hence Mayakkoothan.

Name: Thirukkolur
Note: Birthplace of Madhurakavi Azhwar (Sevvai). The Lord rests on a grain measure, guarding Kubera's lost treasure.

Name: Thirupperai
Note: Nava Tirupati (Sukra). The Lord wears long fish-shaped earrings. Garuda's shrine is set aside so the Lord can watch children at play.

Name: Thirukkurugur
Note: Birthplace of Nammazhwar (Guru). The tamarind tree under which he sat in silence for sixteen years still stands in the temple.

Name: Srivilliputhur
Note: Home of Periyazhwar and his daughter Andal, the only woman among the Azhwars. The garland she wears is sent to Tirumala and Azhagar Koil each year.

Name: Thiruthangal
Note: A hill temple where Sri Devi stayed (thangal) in penance. Linked with the wedding of Aniruddha and Usha.

Name: Thirukkoodal
Note: A three-storey Ashtanga vimanam with the Lord sitting, standing and reclining. Periyazhwar sang Thiruppallandu in this city.

Name: Thirumaliruncholai
Note: Kallazhagar rides to the Vaigai each Chithirai. Andal vowed a hundred pots of sweet rice here, and Ramanuja fulfilled it for her centuries later.

Name: Thirumohur
Note: The Lord took the Mohini form here. Nammazhwar calls Him the guide who walks with the soul on its last journey. The Sudarsana shrine is renowned.

Name: Thirukkoshtiyur
Note: Ramanuja walked here eighteen times to receive the eight-syllable mantra from Thirukoshtiyur Nambi, then shared its meaning openly with all who wished to hear.

Name: Thiruppullani
Perumal: Adi Jagannathan (Kalyana Jagannathan); Darbha Sayana Raman
Note: Sri Rama lay on a bed of darbha grass here for three days, seeking passage from the ocean. Vibhishana's surrender is also placed here.

Name: Thirumeyyam
Note: A rock-cut cave temple with one of the largest reclining forms, carved from the hill itself.

Name: Thiruvayodhi
Note: Birthplace of Sri Rama on the Sarayu. The Azhwars sing the town itself, without naming a single shrine.

Name: Naimisaranyam
Note: The forest itself is worshipped as the Lord. Here Suta Gosvami spoke the Srimad-Bhagavatam to the sages headed by Saunaka.

Name: Thiruppirithi
Note: The first place Thirumangai Azhwar sings in the Periya Thirumozhi. Scholars differ on its exact site, and most pilgrims worship at Joshimath.

Name: Thirukkandam Kadinagar
Note: At the meeting of the Alaknanda and Bhagirathi, where the river is first called Ganga. Periyazhwar's decad praises the Ganga itself.

Name: Thiruvadari
Note: Narayana sits in meditation as the teacher of the eight-syllable mantra. Open about May to November. Thirumangai Azhwar urges: go while your body still has strength.

Name: Thiruchalagramam
Note: The only Divya Desam outside India, at about 3,700 metres. The Gandaki river is the source of salagrama silas.

Name: Vada Mathura
Note: Birthplace of Sri Krishna. Andal's verses long for Mathura, Vrindavana and Govardhana.

Name: Thiruvaippadi
Note: The cowherd village of Krishna's childhood. Periyazhwar sings as Yasoda, and Andal becomes a gopi of this village in the Thiruppavai.

Name: Thiruthuvarai
Note: Krishna as king of Dvaraka. Andal asks to be taken to the city of the Lord of sixteen thousand queens.

Name: Singavel Kundram
Note: Nine forms of Narasimha across a forested hill range, where He appeared from the pillar for Prahlada. Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu offered prayers here.

Name: Thiruvenkadam
Note: Ten Azhwars sang the Lord of the seven hills. Nammazhwar's surrender, "Agalakillen", is offered at these feet.
